description:
Found by the JMAP-g7wu.2.4.6 do-beads triage 2026-05-13.

## Problem

Space top-level metadata fields (`name`, `description`, `iconBlobId`, `isPublic`, `isPubliclyPreviewable`, etc.) are mutated via the standard RFC 8620 PatchObject path in `handle_space_set`, which dispatches through `update_object` — NOT through `apply_space_patch`. The permission-validation pre-check landed in JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3 (`validate_role_member_ops`) explicitly filters to Role/Member ops and does not cover this path. The `apply_space_patch` call only runs for the semantic mutation keys (addRoles, removeRoles, addMembers, etc., per draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Space/set), not for top-level field assignments.

Net effect: a caller without `manage_space` permission can today successfully mutate a Space's top-level metadata via standard /set update operations.

## Spec authority

draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 (current) at the field definitions for `name`, `description`, `isPublic`, `isPubliclyPreviewable`, etc. carries the marker 'Mutable by members with "manage_space" permission'. This is the normative basis for the gate.

## Acceptance

- handle_space_set's update path (the standard RFC 8620 PatchObject branch, NOT the semantic-mutation-key apply_space_patch path) verifies that the caller holds `manage_space` on the target Space before any top-level metadata field is mutated. Failure produces SetError::Forbidden with a descriptive message.
- Enforcement is BACKEND-CANONICAL (per workspace AGENTS.md 'Caller identity (foundation seam)'). The handler MAY do a defense-in-depth pre-check, but the backend MUST re-verify atomically with the mutation.
- Empty patches (no field changes) are still permitted to non-managers (consistent with RFC 8620 /set's tolerance for no-op updates).
- Tests:
  * Caller with `manage_space` mutates `description` → succeeds, change reflected.
  * Caller without `manage_space` (just `@everyone` role) mutates `description` → SetError::Forbidden, no mutation.
  * Caller without `manage_space` mutates a no-op patch (e.g. {}) → succeeds (or no-op response).
  * Mixed patch (`name` + addMembers in one /set call) → still atomic; if caller lacks `manage_space`, both branches are rejected and rolled back.

## Out of scope

- Extending manage_channels enforcement (separate bead).
- Changing the apply_space_patch path (already gates Role/Member ops correctly under JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3).
- ULID migration (separate bead).
- Spec ambiguity on what 'top-level metadata' includes — assume all RFC 8620 PatchObject paths that target a field NOT exposed via semantic mutation keys.

## Cross-references

- JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3 — Role/Member apply_space_patch with permission/hierarchy validation (the work this gate parallels)
- JMAP-g7wu.2.4.6 — the test-matrix bead this finding came out of
- workspace AGENTS.md 'Caller identity (foundation seam)' — the policy this gate operationalizes
title: Space top-level metadata: enforce manage_space permission gate in handle_space_set
